chapter_name: The World of Metals and Non-Metals
learning_objective: 🎯 Dive into the amazing world of materials to discover why some things are shiny and bendable, while others are dull and break easily!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Metals like iron, gold, and copper are the heavy lifters of science! They are usually shiny, hard, and make a ringing sound when you strike them. They are also amazing at letting heat and electricity flow right through them.

Metals have two cool superpowers. You can hammer them into super thin sheets like aluminum foil (malleability) or stretch them into long, thin wires for your phone chargers (ductility) without breaking them!

Non-metals are the rule-breakers! They can be solids like coal, liquids, or even invisible gases like the oxygen we breathe. They look dull, break easily if hit with a hammer, and do not let electricity pass through them.

fun_activity.title: 🥄 The Spoon Sound Test
fun_activity.instructions: Tap a steel spoon gently against a glass bowl, and then tap a wooden spoon against it. Notice the difference in the ringing sound? That special ringing sound is called being 'sonorous', a key property of metals!

quick_recap: ⭐ Metals are shiny, hard, sonorous, and excellent conductors of heat and electricity.
⭐ Malleability lets us flatten metals, and ductility lets us stretch them into wires.
⭐ Non-metals are mostly dull, brittle, and poor conductors.
